title: Enhancer: A Distribution-Aware Framework with Temporal-Relational Meta-Learning for Stock Prediction

problem.claim: Stock prediction models must adapt to evolving temporal dynamics and relational structures in financial markets.

gap.claim: Existing temporal-relational models struggle with systematic temporal and relational distribution shifts because model training relies on the i.i.d. assumption.

contributions.claim: Introduces Enhancer, a model-agnostic framework for temporal-relational distribution shifts that can be applied to downstream predictors.
Uses a meta-learning architecture with Temporal Meta-Learner and Relational Meta-Learner components.
Introduces Reactive Point Processes Attention for fine-grained temporal information and Approximation-Intervention for relational generalization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the work as pioneering research on temporal-relational distribution shifts in stock prediction and describe Approximation-Intervention as the first method addressing relational distribution shift for quantitative investment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across two tasks and four long-term stock datasets, the authors report average increases of 29.3% in profit ratio and 18.54% in Sharpe ratio over baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Stock prediction supports portfolio management and sustainable profitability.
Financial markets evolve through temporal and relational dynamics.
Temporal-relational models face distribution shifts that undermine the i.i.d. training assumption.
Enhancer addresses these shifts through model-agnostic meta-learning, temporal attention, and relational intervention mechanisms.
Experiments evaluate stock trend prediction and investment recommendation on four long-term datasets, with reported improvements over baselines.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates temporal and relational adaptation into dedicated meta-learners.

interpretation.claim: Separating distinct distribution-shift dimensions may help tailor adaptation mechanisms to each source of change.

application.claim: For systems exposed to multiple evolving structures, consider modular adaptation components aligned with distinct shift dimensions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition helps outside stock prediction or across other types of distribution shift.

source_observation.claim: The reported evaluation covers both trend prediction and investment recommendation.

interpretation.claim: Evaluating related prediction and decision tasks can indicate whether a method's benefits extend beyond a single output objective.

application.claim: When assessing adaptive prediction systems, include downstream decision-oriented tasks alongside predictive benchmarks when applicable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify dataset identities, evaluation protocols, or whether the reported averages are statistically significant.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four dataset identities or their time spans.
The abstract does not describe baseline identities, experimental protocols, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or computational requirements.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported improvements.
